title: MD5 used for a security property
summary: MD5 is used for signatures, collision-resistant integrity, or adversary-controlled identifiers.
applicable_when: MD5 output influences authenticity, integrity, authorization, or identity.
check: Trace every MD5 call to its consumer and distinguish non-security checksums.
indicators: A call path where attacker-controlled data and MD5 affect a security decision.
impact: Collision attacks can let distinct inputs share an accepted digest.
remediation: Replace MD5 with an approved modern hash or a keyed construction when authenticity is required.
false_positives: MD5 is used only for accidental-corruption detection or legacy content addressing.

title: SHA-1 used for signatures or collision resistance
summary: SHA-1 protects a signature, certificate, or collision-sensitive identifier.
applicable_when: SHA-1 output is relied on for collision resistance.
check: Trace SHA-1 outputs into signature or identity checks.
indicators: A SHA-1 algorithm identifier or call on an attacker-influenceable signed object.
impact: Practical collisions can undermine authenticity or identity binding.
remediation: Migrate to SHA-256 or a stronger approved hash and reissue affected signatures.
false_positives: SHA-1 is used inside an approved legacy construction whose threat model does not require collision resistance.

title: Single DES or two-key TDEA remains in use
summary: A legacy 56-bit DES-strength construction protects live data.
applicable_when: DES or two-key TDEA is used beyond decoding historical data.
check: Identify algorithm negotiation and all encrypting call sites.
indicators: DES/TDEA keys, OIDs, cipher names, or live ciphertext generation.
impact: The effective key strength permits feasible recovery and legacy modes add structural weaknesses.
remediation: Migrate to an approved AEAD such as AES-GCM with a suitable key size.

title: Three-key TDEA used for new protection
summary: Three-key TDEA is still used to encrypt new data despite its retired status and small block size.
applicable_when: New records are protected with three-key TDEA.
check: Trace encryption timestamps and algorithm selection.
indicators: A live encryption path selecting three-key TDEA.
impact: Limited security strength and 64-bit block collisions constrain safe data volumes.
remediation: Migrate to AES-based authenticated encryption and decrypt or rewrap retained data.

title: RC4 protects confidentiality
summary: RC4 is used to encrypt attacker-observable or attacker-influenceable data.
applicable_when: RC4 or an RC4-compatible implementation is active.
check: Identify KSA/PRGA code or library selection and confirm live use.
indicators: RC4 state initialization plus a caller that emits protected traffic.
impact: Keystream biases and protocol interactions can disclose plaintext.
remediation: Replace RC4 with a modern AEAD construction.

title: ECDSA/DSA signing nonce repeats
summary: Two signatures under one private key use the same per-message nonce.
applicable_when: DSA or ECDSA signs more than one message.
check: Compare signature r values and trace nonce generation across failures and cloning.
indicators: Repeated r under one key or a reachable nonce-state reset.
impact: A pair of signatures can reveal the private signing key.
remediation: Use an approved deterministic or robust randomized nonce-generation process.

title: ECDSA/DSA signing nonce is biased or predictable
summary: Per-message nonces lack sufficient entropy or leak partial information.
applicable_when: DSA or ECDSA signatures are attacker-observable.
check: Inspect nonce generation and statistically or side-channel assess leakage.
indicators: Predictable seed, modulo bias, truncated entropy, or partial nonce leakage.
impact: Lattice and related attacks can recover the private key.
remediation: Use approved nonce generation and a side-channel-resistant implementation.

title: Peer elliptic-curve public key is not validated
summary: Key agreement accepts invalid points, wrong subgroups, or disallowed curves without required checks.
applicable_when: Untrusted peers supply EC public values.
check: Trace decoding, curve selection, on-curve/subgroup checks, and all-zero handling.
indicators: Malformed or small-order public values reach scalar multiplication or derived keys.
impact: Invalid-curve or subgroup attacks may disclose private scalars or force known secrets.
remediation: Apply the validation rules required by the chosen curve and protocol.

title: X25519/X448 all-zero shared secret is accepted
summary: A low-order input produces an all-zero output that continues into key derivation as if secret.
applicable_when: X25519 or X448 processes untrusted public inputs.
check: Trace the shared-secret result check before the KDF.
indicators: All-zero output accepted and used as session key material.
impact: An attacker can force a predictable shared secret and bypass peer contribution.
remediation: Reject the all-zero output when the protocol requires contributory behavior.

title: Key agreement omits identity or transcript binding
summary: A DH/ECDH secret is derived without binding both roles, public keys, algorithms, and protocol transcript.
applicable_when: Unauthenticated or separately authenticated key agreement establishes sessions.
check: Map authenticated context into the KDF and confirmation messages.
indicators: Session keys derived only from the mathematical shared secret.
impact: Unknown-key-share, role-confusion, or downgrade attacks may bind keys to the wrong peer or context.
remediation: Bind identities, roles, public values, algorithms, and transcript into derivation or key confirmation.

title: Password used directly as a cryptographic key
summary: Password bytes, a simple encoding, or a single fast hash become an encryption or MAC key.
applicable_when: Human-memorable input protects encrypted data or authentication verifiers.
check: Trace password processing to the final key import.
indicators: Direct bytes or one fast digest used as key material.
impact: Offline guessing is inexpensive and limited by password entropy.
remediation: Use a salted, tunable password KDF with parameters appropriate to the platform.

title: Password KDF work factor is too low
summary: PBKDF parameters permit inexpensive offline guesses for the deployment and date.
applicable_when: An attacker can obtain a verifier or encrypted object for offline testing.
check: Extract algorithm and all cost parameters and benchmark representative hardware.
indicators: A low iteration, memory, or parallelism cost relative to current policy.
impact: Attackers can test large password dictionaries cheaply.
remediation: Raise tunable costs and support parameter upgrades on successful authentication.

title: Password KDF uses a missing or reused salt
summary: Password-derived outputs are unsalted or share a fixed/global salt across principals.
applicable_when: Passwords are hashed or derive stored encryption keys.
check: Trace salt generation, storage, length, and per-record uniqueness.
indicators: Empty, constant, username-only, or repeated salt values.
impact: Equal passwords share outputs and precomputation amortizes attacks.
remediation: Generate a unique random salt per password-derived record and store it with parameters.

title: Password KDF parameters are not authenticated or bounded
summary: Attacker-controlled cost, salt, or algorithm metadata can weaken derivation or cause resource exhaustion.
applicable_when: Serialized password-protected data supplies KDF parameters.
check: Trace parameter parsing, bounds, and integrity protection.
indicators: Untrusted parameters accepted without minimums, maximums, or authenticated binding.
impact: Attackers may downgrade protection or trigger denial of service.
remediation: Authenticate parameters and enforce algorithm-specific safe bounds before derivation.

title: Raw shared secret is used directly
summary: A Diffie-Hellman or KEM shared secret becomes an application key without extraction and context binding.
applicable_when: Key establishment returns nonuniform or context-free shared secret material.
check: Trace established secrets to encryption, MAC, and export APIs.
indicators: Direct truncation or direct key import of the raw shared secret.
impact: Bias, cross-protocol reuse, and missing transcript binding can weaken session keys.
remediation: Apply an approved extract-and-expand KDF with protocol context and independent labels.

title: KDF lacks domain separation
summary: The same inputs derive keys for different directions, algorithms, roles, or protocol versions without distinct labels.
applicable_when: One root secret produces multiple operational keys.
check: Compare KDF inputs and labels across every derived key.
indicators: Identical context/label inputs for distinct purposes.
impact: Keys can coincide or be substituted across protocol roles.
remediation: Bind purpose, direction, identities, algorithm, and version into unambiguous KDF context.

title: HKDF extract step is skipped with weak input
summary: HKDF-Expand or equivalent is applied directly to a low-entropy, biased, or attacker-influenced secret.
applicable_when: Input keying material is not already a uniformly random pseudorandom key.
check: Trace whether extraction precedes expansion and assess input distribution.
indicators: Expand-only derivation from a DH value, password, or composite secret without justification.
impact: The KDF may not achieve the expected pseudorandomness or entropy concentration.
remediation: Use HKDF-Extract with an appropriate salt before expansion.

title: Hardcoded secret key
summary: A reusable symmetric or private key is embedded in distributable code, firmware, configuration, or resources.
applicable_when: An artifact delivered outside the trust boundary contains key material.
check: Follow candidate constants into key-import or signing APIs.
indicators: A byte sequence or encoded key at a reproducible location used by a cryptographic operation.
impact: Anyone with the artifact can recover the key and impersonate peers or decrypt protected data.
remediation: Provision unique keys through a protected enrollment and storage mechanism.

title: Fleet-wide shared key
summary: The same long-lived secret is reused across users, tenants, devices, or installations.
applicable_when: Multiple security principals use one symmetric or private key.
check: Compare provisioning flows and keys across at least two principals.
indicators: Identical key identifiers/material or a single global key lookup for distinct principals.
impact: One compromise expands to every principal sharing the key.
remediation: Generate and manage distinct keys per security domain, with scoped derivation where appropriate.

title: One key reused across cryptographic purposes
summary: A key serves incompatible roles such as encryption and MAC, signing and key agreement, or production and test.
applicable_when: One key identifier reaches more than one primitive or protocol purpose.
check: Build a use map from each key origin to all consumers.
indicators: The same key bytes or handle enter operations with distinct purposes.
impact: Cross-protocol interactions can invalidate security assumptions and broaden compromise impact.
remediation: Derive or provision independent purpose-bound keys with explicit labels.

title: Key lacks rotation or cryptoperiod enforcement
summary: A long-lived key remains active indefinitely or beyond its designed data/use limit.
applicable_when: Persistent keys protect ongoing operations.
check: Inspect creation, activation, expiry, rotation, and retirement paths.
indicators: No expiry metadata, unreachable rotation code, or use continuing beyond policy.
impact: Exposure accumulates over time and algorithm-specific usage bounds may be exceeded.
remediation: Define and enforce cryptoperiods, rotation, rekeying, and retirement.

title: Retired key remains usable
summary: Revoked, expired, or replaced key material can still authorize new operations.
applicable_when: The system supports key retirement or revocation.
check: Test callers and caches after the key state changes.
indicators: A successful new cryptographic operation using a retired key.
impact: Compromised or superseded credentials retain authority.
remediation: Enforce key state at every use point and invalidate distributed caches atomically.

title: Secret key stored without adequate protection
summary: Private or symmetric keys are persisted in plaintext or under protections available to the same attacker.
applicable_when: Long-term secret material is stored outside a dedicated protected boundary.
check: Trace serialization, filesystem permissions, wrapping keys, and backup copies.
indicators: Plaintext key bytes or reversibly encoded material in accessible storage.
impact: Local disclosure, backup access, or artifact theft becomes full key compromise.
remediation: Use platform-backed secret storage or properly separated key wrapping and least privilege.

title: Key wrapping lacks integrity
summary: Exported or stored keys are encrypted without binding metadata and detecting modification.
applicable_when: Keys leave their generating module or are stored wrapped.
check: Inspect the wrapping construction, authenticated metadata, and unwrap errors.
indicators: A malleable encryption-only wrapper or unauthenticated algorithm/key identifiers.
impact: Attackers may substitute, alter, or relabel wrapped keys.
remediation: Use an approved authenticated key-wrapping construction and bind key attributes.

title: Key generation bypasses approved generation process
summary: Key bytes are chosen, truncated, or transformed outside the prescribed generator.
applicable_when: The target creates cryptographic keys.
check: Trace entropy through generation, validation, and import.
indicators: Direct use of arbitrary bytes, identifiers, timestamps, or truncated outputs as keys.
impact: Effective key strength can be far below the algorithm's nominal strength.
remediation: Use an approved key-generation process with sufficient entropy and validation.

title: Key material crosses trust boundaries unnecessarily
summary: Secret keys are exported, logged, copied, or delivered to components that do not require them.
applicable_when: A key is available through an API or shared among processes.
check: Map every serialization and recipient of key material.
indicators: An export path or broad key read permission without a cryptographic need.
impact: Additional copies and principals increase disclosure opportunities and complicate revocation.
remediation: Keep keys non-exportable where possible and expose narrow cryptographic operations instead.

title: Key destruction is incomplete
summary: Superseded secrets remain in files, caches, backups, swap, or process memory beyond operational need.
applicable_when: Secret material is retired or temporary.
check: Inspect cleanup paths and all copies created during import and use.
indicators: Recoverable retired key bytes or omitted cleanup for owned buffers/files.
impact: Later memory or storage disclosure recovers credentials believed destroyed.
remediation: Minimize copies and apply platform-appropriate secure destruction and retention controls.

title: Unkeyed hash substitutes for a MAC
summary: A digest over message fields is treated as proof of authenticity.
applicable_when: Attackers can modify both data and its digest.
check: Trace verification and identify whether a secret key enters the construction.
indicators: A plain hash or checksum accepted as an authenticator.
impact: Anyone who changes the message can recompute the digest.
remediation: Use HMAC, KMAC, or an appropriate protocol-defined authenticator.

title: Secret-prefix Merkle-Damgard MAC permits length extension
summary: The authenticator is Hash(secret || message) using an extensible hash construction.
applicable_when: The hash and message length permit length-extension behavior.
check: Identify concatenation order and test extension against verification.
indicators: A raw secret-prefix SHA-2/MD5/SHA-1 digest used as MAC.
impact: Attackers may append data and compute a valid digest without the secret.
remediation: Use HMAC or another standardized MAC.

title: Authenticator comparison leaks timing
summary: MACs, tags, tokens, or password-derived values are compared with early exit on secret-dependent bytes.
applicable_when: An attacker can repeat measurements with controlled candidates.
check: Inspect comparison primitive and measure position-dependent timing.
indicators: memcmp/string equality or a loop that returns at the first mismatch.
impact: Timing samples may reveal a valid authenticator incrementally.
remediation: Use a constant-time comparison with fixed-length validation.

title: MAC key is too short or derived from low entropy
summary: The key's effective entropy is below the intended authentication strength.
applicable_when: A MAC relies on a password, identifier, or truncated source.
check: Trace key origin and entropy, not just buffer length.
indicators: Low-entropy input or excessive truncation feeding the MAC key.
impact: Attackers can guess the key offline and forge arbitrary messages.
remediation: Generate or derive an independent MAC key with sufficient entropy.

title: MAC does not bind message framing
summary: Ambiguous concatenation of fields lets different semantic messages share one authenticated byte string.
applicable_when: Multiple fields or types are concatenated before authentication.
check: Reconstruct encodings and search for ambiguous boundaries or alternate canonical forms.
indicators: Two distinct parsed messages mapping to the same authenticated representation.
impact: Attackers can substitute meanings without breaking the MAC.
remediation: Use an unambiguous canonical encoding with lengths/types included in authenticated data.

title: ML-KEM decapsulation failure is distinguishable
summary: Failure behavior reveals whether a ciphertext was valid instead of applying the required implicit-rejection behavior.
applicable_when: ML-KEM or another implicit-rejection KEM decapsulates attacker input.
check: Compare returned secrets, errors, timing, and protocol behavior for malformed ciphertexts.
indicators: Validity-dependent errors, timing, or omission of a fallback secret.
impact: Chosen-ciphertext queries may undermine KEM security or create protocol oracles.
remediation: Use the standardized decapsulation algorithm and keep failure behavior indistinguishable.

title: KEM shared secret is used without context-bound derivation
summary: A KEM output is directly used as a traffic key or combined ambiguously with other secrets.
applicable_when: A KEM establishes an application or hybrid session secret.
check: Trace shared secret through combination, extraction, transcript binding, and labels.
indicators: Direct key import or ambiguous concatenation of KEM/classical secrets.
impact: Cross-protocol, downgrade, and hybrid-composition assumptions may fail.
remediation: Apply a protocol-specified KDF that binds the complete transcript, roles, algorithms, and component secrets.

title: KEM public key is not bound to the intended recipient
summary: Encapsulation uses an unauthenticated, substituted, or ambiguously identified public key.
applicable_when: A peer KEM public key arrives over an attacker-influenceable channel.
check: Trace certificate, pin, signature, or authenticated transcript binding.
indicators: A KEM key accepted without authenticating its owner and intended role.
impact: Attackers can substitute a key and terminate confidentiality to themselves.
remediation: Authenticate the KEM public key and bind its algorithm and role into the protocol.

title: Unsupported or nonstandard PQC parameters are accepted
summary: The implementation accepts altered parameter sets, draft identifiers, or unvalidated variants as production algorithms.
applicable_when: PQC algorithm identifiers or parameters are negotiated or parsed.
check: Enumerate accepted identifiers, sizes, parameter sets, and downgrade behavior.
indicators: Acceptance of draft/unknown parameters or mismatch with the deployed standard.
impact: Security strength and interoperability assumptions may be invalid or attacker-controlled.
remediation: Allow only explicitly supported standardized parameter sets and authenticate negotiation.

title: Hybrid key establishment silently loses one component
summary: Failure, downgrade, or parser behavior can omit the classical or post-quantum secret without detection.
applicable_when: A hybrid construction combines two or more key-establishment mechanisms.
check: Force each component to fail or disappear and inspect transcript and derived-key changes.
indicators: Session success with a missing component where policy requires both.
impact: The session may provide only the weaker component's security while appearing hybrid.
remediation: Use a specified combiner, bind the suite and both contributions, and fail when required components are absent.

title: Non-cryptographic PRNG generates secrets
summary: A predictable generator such as an LCG, Mersenne Twister, rand(), or Math.random() creates keys, nonces, tokens, or challenges.
applicable_when: Random-looking values protect a security property.
check: Trace generator identity and every seed source.
indicators: A non-cryptographic generator feeding security-sensitive output.
impact: Observed outputs or guessed state can predict future or reconstruct past secrets.
remediation: Use the operating system CSPRNG or an approved DRBG correctly seeded with entropy.

title: Predictable seed initializes a DRBG or PRNG
summary: Time, PID, device identifiers, counters, or other guessable values supply the effective seed.
applicable_when: A deterministic generator produces security-sensitive values.
check: Reconstruct seed material and estimate attacker-visible uncertainty.
indicators: A seed composed only of predictable or low-entropy values.
impact: Attackers can enumerate generator state and derive secrets.
remediation: Seed from an approved entropy source with the required entropy strength.

title: DRBG state is cloned across instances
summary: Forks, VM snapshots, containers, or copied persistent state produce identical random streams.
applicable_when: A stateful generator survives process cloning, fork, snapshot, or image creation.
check: Compare output across cloned instances and inspect reseed-on-fork behavior.
indicators: Repeated streams or identical internal state after cloning.
impact: Keys and nonces can collide across otherwise independent principals.
remediation: Detect cloning/fork events and reseed from fresh entropy before generating output.

title: DRBG is not reseeded after entropy or usage limits
summary: A long-running generator exceeds its reseed interval or cannot recover after state compromise.
applicable_when: A DRBG runs for long periods or generates high volumes.
check: Inspect reseed counters, entropy callbacks, and error paths.
indicators: Generation continues after the designed reseed interval or failed reseed.
impact: Security guarantees degrade and compromise recovery may be impossible.
remediation: Enforce reseed intervals and fail safely when fresh entropy is unavailable.

title: Entropy-source failure is ignored
summary: Startup or runtime entropy health failures fall back to weak values or continue silently.
applicable_when: The platform can report entropy or DRBG initialization failure.
check: Force and trace entropy-source error paths.
indicators: A success return, fallback constant, or continued generation after entropy failure.
impact: All downstream keys and nonces may be predictable without visible failure.
remediation: Propagate failure, stop secret generation, and surface an operational fault.

title: Random output is reused as multiple independent secrets
summary: One random value is copied into keys, IVs, salts, tokens, or protocol challenges without derivation labels.
applicable_when: A random seed or buffer feeds multiple security roles.
check: Map slices and copies of each random output to consumers.
indicators: The same bytes used in independent roles.
impact: Role correlation and cross-protocol behavior can undermine independent security assumptions.
remediation: Generate independent values or derive labeled outputs with a suitable KDF.

title: Insufficient entropy for requested security strength
summary: The generator or entropy source cannot supply uncertainty commensurate with produced keys.
applicable_when: High-strength keys are generated from a constrained or biased source.
check: Estimate min-entropy and inspect conditioning and startup collection.
indicators: Documented or measured entropy below the requested strength.
impact: Brute-force cost is determined by entropy, not nominal key length.
remediation: Use a validated entropy source and generation process sized for the target strength.

title: Textbook RSA operation protects application data
summary: Raw modular exponentiation is used without a standardized encryption or signature encoding.
applicable_when: Application data reaches RSA primitives directly.
check: Trace big-integer exponentiation inputs and look for OAEP/PSS encoding.
indicators: RSAEP/RSADP or RSASP1/RSAVP1 used on raw application values.
impact: Determinism and algebraic malleability destroy standard confidentiality or signature guarantees.
remediation: Use RSA-OAEP for encryption and RSA-PSS for new signature designs, within a defined protocol.

title: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption exposes an oracle
summary: Validity, timing, or downstream behavior distinguishes correctly encoded RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 plaintext.
applicable_when: An attacker can submit chosen RSA ciphertexts.
check: Compare all decryption failures, timing, and generated fallback secrets.
indicators: A distinguishable padding result or application behavior correlated with validity.
impact: Adaptive queries can recover plaintext or session keys.
remediation: Migrate to OAEP or a KEM; until then implement protocol-specific implicit rejection and uniform behavior.

title: RSA-OAEP parameters disagree or are weakly bound
summary: Hash, MGF hash, label, or algorithm identifiers differ across endpoints or are attacker-selectable.
applicable_when: RSA-OAEP is used with configurable or serialized parameters.
check: Inspect both encode/decode parameter sets and authenticated algorithm negotiation.
indicators: Parameter mismatch, weak hash selection, or unauthenticated identifiers.
impact: Interoperability failures can become downgrade or oracle surfaces.
remediation: Fix and authenticate OAEP parameters according to the protocol profile.

title: RSA signature verification accepts malformed encoding
summary: Verification parses PKCS#1 v1.5 or PSS encoding leniently, incompletely, or with trailing data.
applicable_when: Custom or low-level RSA signature verification exists.
check: Test malformed DigestInfo, padding length, trailing bytes, and PSS parameters.
indicators: A malformed encoded message accepted as a valid signature.
impact: Attackers may forge signatures by exploiting parser/verifier discrepancies.
remediation: Use a maintained high-level verification API and enforce the complete encoding specification.

title: RSA modulus or key generation is too weak
summary: RSA uses an undersized modulus, defective primes, shared factors, or noncompliant generation.
applicable_when: RSA keys are generated or accepted.
check: Measure modulus size, batch-GCD public keys, and inspect generation validation.
indicators: A modulus below policy strength, shared factor, or invalid key parameters.
impact: Factoring or shared-prime recovery reveals private keys.
remediation: Generate compliant keys with an approved generator and reject inadequate imported keys.

title: RSA private operation lacks blinding or fault verification
summary: Secret exponentiation is directly exposed to timing, power, cache, or induced-fault observations.
applicable_when: Attackers can measure or perturb private-key operations.
check: Inspect blinding, CRT recombination checks, and error handling.
indicators: Unblinded private operation or CRT result returned without verification.
impact: Side channels or one faulty signature can reveal the private key.
remediation: Use a hardened library with blinding and verify CRT results before release.

title: Signature verification result is ignored or inverted
summary: The application proceeds when verification fails, errors, or is never called.
applicable_when: Signed input controls a security decision.
check: Trace every verifier return and exceptional path into authorization/use.
indicators: Unchecked return, fail-open exception, or inverted boolean/error code.
impact: Attackers can supply modified or unsigned content as authentic.
remediation: Make verification success an explicit prerequisite and fail closed on every other result.

title: Signature omits security-critical context
summary: Only payload bytes are signed while identity, version, algorithm, destination, or framing remains mutable.
applicable_when: Unsigned metadata changes the interpretation of signed content.
check: Reconstruct the exact signed byte string and parser inputs.
indicators: Mutable security-relevant fields outside the signature.
impact: Valid signatures can be replayed, relabeled, downgraded, or interpreted in another protocol.
remediation: Sign an unambiguous, domain-separated encoding of payload and required context.

title: Non-canonical signature or key encodings create ambiguity
summary: Multiple byte encodings of one value are accepted across components with different semantics.
applicable_when: Signatures or public keys traverse multiple parsers or identity stores.
check: Test non-minimal integers, alternate DER, malleable forms, and normalization.
indicators: Distinct encodings accepted as equivalent in one component but distinct in another.
impact: Attackers may bypass deduplication, caching, policy, or transaction identity.
remediation: Require one canonical encoding before verification and downstream identity decisions.

title: ECB mode reveals plaintext structure
summary: A deterministic block-by-block mode protects more than one block of structured data.
applicable_when: ECB encrypts attacker-observable data.
check: Inspect mode constants and compare repeated ciphertext blocks.
indicators: ECB selection or equal plaintext blocks producing equal ciphertext blocks.
impact: Patterns, equality, and repeated fields remain visible.
remediation: Use an authenticated encryption mode with a unique nonce.

title: CBC uses a fixed or repeated IV
summary: More than one message under a CBC key uses the same IV.
applicable_when: CBC encrypts multiple messages under one key.
check: Trace IV origin and compare records across restarts and concurrency.
indicators: A constant, deterministic repetition, or observed duplicate IV under one key.
impact: First-block equality leaks and chosen-plaintext attacks may become possible.
remediation: Generate an unpredictable fresh IV for each CBC encryption and transmit it with the ciphertext.

title: CTR or stream-cipher nonce repeats
summary: Two plaintexts are encrypted under the same key and counter/nonce stream position.
applicable_when: CTR or a stream cipher protects multiple messages.
check: Construct key/nonce pairs from traces and inspect persistence and concurrency.
indicators: A repeated key/nonce pair or counter reset path.
impact: XOR of ciphertexts reveals XOR of plaintexts and can lead to plaintext recovery.
remediation: Guarantee unique nonces/counters per key across restart, rollback, and concurrency.

title: Encryption lacks authenticity
summary: Malleable encryption is accepted without a MAC or AEAD tag covering ciphertext and context.
applicable_when: Attackers can alter encrypted records.
check: Trace decrypt callers and all integrity checks before plaintext use.
indicators: CBC, CTR, or stream ciphertext accepted without a cryptographic authenticator.
impact: Attackers can modify plaintext or construct chosen-ciphertext oracles.
remediation: Use an AEAD construction or a rigorously composed encrypt-then-MAC design.

title: MAC-then-encrypt exposes padding or format oracles
summary: Authentication is checked only after unauthenticated decryption and distinguishable parsing.
applicable_when: A padded encryption scheme authenticates plaintext rather than ciphertext.
check: Compare error, timing, and network behavior for malformed ciphertexts.
indicators: Distinct padding/MAC outcomes or plaintext processing before authentication.
impact: Adaptive queries can recover plaintext or forge records.
remediation: Prefer AEAD; otherwise authenticate ciphertext before decryption and unify failure behavior.

title: GCM nonce repeats under one key
summary: The same GCM invocation nonce is used more than once with a key.
applicable_when: GCM encrypts or authenticates multiple messages under one key.
check: Trace nonce construction across threads, crashes, restore, and key rotation; compare captures.
indicators: A repeated key/nonce pair or a reachable generator collision/reset.
impact: Confidentiality degrades and authentication forgeries can become practical.
remediation: Enforce per-key nonce uniqueness with a robust counter or another approved construction.

title: AEAD tag is truncated below justified strength
summary: The implementation accepts tags shorter than the protocol's required security bound.
applicable_when: An AEAD or MAC tag length is configurable or encoded in input.
check: Find accepted tag lengths and estimate attempts permitted per key.
indicators: Acceptance of an unexpectedly short tag without strict attempt/data limits.
impact: Online forgery probability rises and may become operationally exploitable.
remediation: Use the full recommended tag or a rigorously bounded protocol-approved truncation.

title: AEAD associated data omits security-critical context
summary: Ciphertext authenticates payload but not routing, identity, version, sequence, or algorithm metadata that affects interpretation.
applicable_when: Unauthenticated metadata changes how decrypted plaintext is processed.
check: Map every security-relevant field into AEAD AAD or the encrypted plaintext.
indicators: Mutable metadata outside tag coverage that changes authorization or semantics.
impact: Attackers can relabel, replay, redirect, or reinterpret valid ciphertext.
remediation: Authenticate all context required to bind ciphertext to its intended protocol meaning.

title: Plaintext is released before AEAD verification
summary: Streaming or error paths expose decrypted bytes before the final tag succeeds.
applicable_when: The AEAD API permits incremental plaintext output.
check: Trace buffer visibility and callbacks before final verification.
indicators: Caller-consumed plaintext or side effects preceding tag success.
impact: Modified ciphertext can influence parsing or state despite eventual authentication failure.
remediation: Buffer plaintext privately and release it only after successful final verification.
